The negative branch (unknown collection -> 404) was never exercised. The flagged DEFECT lines concern a DIFFERENT face than the quoted assertion governs: the global GET /aliases face, whose own documented semantics is 'across all collections' — the extra row sem_gdc1_al_1929a5ad belongs to a pre-existing foreign collection, so the per-collection listing behavior asserted by the constraint was never violated (the observed mismatching face lies outside the quoted constraint's domain; the constraint citation is the one the script itself declares).

chain_trace.break_detail: The DEFECT verdicts do not follow from the raw evidence: all 22 raw responses (5 alias ops + per-collection face reads + global reads) are mutually consistent and match the source implementation and the doc corpus exactly. The only difference between each 'listing' and each 'expected' dict is the row sem_gdc1_al_1929a5ad -> sem_gdc1_81ce0571, an alias on a collection this script never created or touched: it is already present in state_aliases_collection_list_002's earlier run of the same session (timestamps ...859 vs ...862) and no script in this session creates it, proving it is leftover state in a shared/persistent qdrant instance. GET /aliases is documented and implemented as a union across ALL collections, so the global listing was correct; the script's expectation (global == this script's aliases only) has no grounding in the cited constraint (which governs only the per-collection face) nor in the doc. Additionally the contract link is weak: the dispatch constraint_id is empty. The per-collection unit under the constraint passed in every phase.

source_grounding.source_excerpt: lib/storage/src/content_manager/alias_mapping.rs:15-16: #[derive(...)] pub struct AliasMapping(HashMap<Alias, CollectionId>)  -- single GLOBAL alias->collection map, one row per alias name instance-wide; :66-70 pub fn insert(&mut self, alias: String, collection_name: String) -> Result<(), StorageError> { self.alias_mapping.0.insert(alias, collection_name); self.alias_mapping.save(&self.data_path)?; Ok(()) } (plain HashMap overwrite => create_alias is an upsert); :114-122 pub fn collection_aliases(&self, collection_name: &str) -> Vec<String> { let mut result = vec![]; for (alias, target_collection) in self.alias_mapping.0.iter() { if collection_name == target_collection { result.push(alias.clone()); } } result } -- per-collection face = rows whose target equals the queried collection (can never show a foreign row, a duplicate, or a row with a different collection_name). lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/mod.rs:452-469: /// List of all aliases across all collections; pub async fn list_aliases(&self, access: &Access) -> Result<Vec<AliasDescription>, StorageError> { let all_collections = self.all_collections(access).await; let mut aliases: Vec<AliasDescription> = Default::default(); for collection_pass in &all_collections { for alias in self.collection_aliases(collection_pass, access).await? { aliases.push(AliasDescription { alias_name: alias.clone(), collection_name: collection_pass.to_string() }); } } Ok(aliases) } -- GET /aliases iterates EVERY existing collection, i.e. a union across all collections; a leftover alias on any other existing collection (sem_gdc1_81ce0571) necessarily appears. src/common/collections.rs:167-188 do_list_collection_aliases maps the per-collection alias set into CollectionsAliasesResponse { aliases } with collection_name = the queried collection.
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases (collections_api.rs:94-109) -> do_list_collection_aliases (common/collections.rs:167-188) -> toc.collection_aliases (toc/mod.rs:434-450) -> alias_persistence.collection_aliases filter by target==queried collection (alias_mapping.rs:114-122). actix GET /aliases (collections_api.rs:48-57) -> do_list_aliases (common/collections.rs:190-196) -> toc.list_aliases (toc/mod.rs:453-469) -> per-collection alias reads over all_collections. Alias writes POST /collections/aliases -> update_aliases -> alias_mapping.insert/remove (plain HashMap ops, alias_mapping.rs:66-93): duplicate create_alias overwrites the same row (idempotent), rebind overwrites the single row of the same alias name (no residue possible on the old target because membership is one global row per alias), delete removes the row. Every observed raw response in the log is exactly what this code produces; there is no code path under which the claimed 'cross-face drift' (global listing showing a legitimately-existing foreign alias) could be a server-side anomaly.
